result.summary: Full S1-S14 gate for REQ-024 (`/my` registrations view: live status, computed waitlist position, QR pass). Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md in full, then the actual diff myself (`git diff master...HEAD`) rather than trusting BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's reports. Files read directly: apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts (full), apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts (full), apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (the new getMyRegistrations block, full withdrawRegistration/decideWithdrawOutcome for the adversarial scenario), apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts (full, to confirm byte-identity), apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts / i18n/en.ts / i18n/ru.ts / i18n/types.ts / index.ts / package.json diffs, apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts and handlers/my.test.ts in full. S3 (primary focus) -- own adversarial scenario, beyond REVIEWER's fixture: built a fresh victim/attacker fixture (victim fully profiled -- firstName/lastName/company/phone/email -- admitted registration with a real qr_token; attacker a separate real bot user who never registered for anything and never received /my's own rendered button). Dispatched a FORGED `withdraw:confirm:` callback_query from the attacker via real `bot.handleUpdate()` against the unchanged `makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler`. Traced the mechanism first: `withdrawRegistration` (domain/registration.ts:499-565) re-reads the row fresh inside its own transaction by id alone (`WHERE registrations.id = registrationId FOR UPDATE`, no userId filter in the WHERE clause) and only THEN calls the pure `decideWithdrawOutcome`, whose ownership check (`ownerUserId !== actingUserId` -> `not-owner`) runs after that identical read regardless of whether the id is real-but-not-owned or simply nonexistent -- so the code path length/shape is identical for both cases (one SELECT FOR UPDATE, one sync decision, no write), giving no structural timing distinguisher. `withdraw.ts`'s confirm handler's switch then maps BOTH `not-owner` and `not-found` to the exact same string, `catalog.withdraw.refusedNotFound` (handlers/withdraw.ts, the switch's `case 'not-owner'` comment: 'One generic string -- same non-disclosure discipline resolveActingUser's other callers already follow'). I verified this holds, not just read it: ran the forged-callback update against a real-but-other-user id and against a syntactically-identical bogus UUID and asserted the two full captured Telegram payload sets (`sendMessage` text) are byte-equal, that neither contains any of the victim's PII strings (name/company/phone/email), and that the victim's registration row was unmodified (still `admitted`) after the forged call -- all three assertions passed against real Postgres via `npx vitest run` on an ad hoc scratch test file (written, run, and deleted after use per file-placement rules -- not committed). This confirms REQ-022's already-reviewed guarantee transfers unchanged to /my's reuse of the same callback pattern: the handler is content-addressed by callback_data alone and structurally cannot tell, or leak, whether an id belongs to the caller, another real user, or nobody -- exactly because `withdraw.ts` is byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts` produces zero output). QR-content-leak check (new for this requirement): read `domain/qr.ts` in full -- `renderCheckInQrPng` composes exactly `https://t.me/?start=ci_` from its two input parameters, nothing else; no `db`/`ctx`/profile lookup in this module at all (framework-free per decisions/0004, confirmed by its own import list: only `qrcode`). `apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts` decodes the ACTUAL produced PNG bytes with a real decoder (jsqr + pngjs, not a re-inspection of the encoder's input string) and asserts the decoded text equals that exact template -- re-ran this test myself (`npx vitest run`, passed). The caption sent alongside the photo (`handlers/my.ts` step 5f) is the row's own composed text (status label, event title, date/time, optional waitlist line) -- all fields already scoped to the viewer's own row per S3, no other-user data, no raw qr_token or any other secret rendered as visible text anywhere in the caption. Confirmed no second encoding path exists: `renderCheckInQrPng` is the QR module's only export, called from exactly one call site in `my.ts`. Third-party dependency risk (`qrcode` 1.5.4, `jsqr` 1.4.0 devDep, `pngjs` 7.0.0 devDep + `@types/*`): ran `npm audit` (repo root, both default and `--omit=dev`) against npm's registry advisory database -- 0 vulnerabilities found for the full dependency tree including these new packages. This is a real check, not skipped as out-of-scope, though it is bounded to what npm's advisory feed currently knows; noting for future dependency-audit tooling (this project has none dedicated beyond `npm audit`) that a periodic re-run is the only way this stays current as new CVEs are disclosed. `jsqr`/`pngjs` are devDependencies only (test-time QR decoding), not shipped in the bot's runtime dependency set beyond `pngjs` overlapping as `qrcode`'s own transitive dep (`qrcode@1.5.4 -> pngjs@5.0.0`, distinct from the project's own pinned devDep `pngjs@7.0.0` -- two coexisting versions, expected and harmless, confirmed via `npm ls qrcode jsqr pngjs -w apps/bot`). Withdraw-button reuse confirmed genuinely risk-free: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts` is empty (byte-for-byte unchanged) -- re-ran this myself, matches REVIEWER's report exactly. `/my`'s only touch on the withdraw surface is emitting the same `withdraw:confirm:` string into a button (`handlers/my.ts` line ~103), registered against the exact same pre-existing handler in `index.ts` (confirmed: `index.ts`'s diff adds only the new `bot.command('my', ...)` registration, no change to the existing `bot.callbackQuery(WITHDRAW_CONFIRM_PATTERN, ...)` line). Remaining S1-S14 items, each re-derived against this diff specifically: - S1 (consent precedes storage): N/A -- this diff performs no writes to User/Profile consent columns; `getMyRegistrations` is a pure SELECT, confirmed by reading its full body (one query, `.map` over rows, no `.insert`/`.update`). - S2 (authorization on the action, negative path proven): applies as 'any authenticated member may read their own data via /my, no organizer/staff gate needed' -- correct per the requirement's own nature (self-read, not cross-user). Verified via S3's adversarial test above that the one action reachable from /my's rendered UI (withdraw) still enforces ownership on the actual write path, not just the button's visibility. - S4 (tokens unguessable, single-purpose): no new token generation in this diff -- `qr_token` values are read-only here, generated unchanged by REQ-020/023's `generateQrToken` (untouched, confirmed no diff to that function). The QR image is a new *rendering* of an existing token, not a new token; confirmed it authorizes nothing beyond identifying a registration at check-in (§2's own stated scope boundary: decode-side is explicitly out of scope, `/checkin` never modified here -- confirmed `handlers/checkin.ts` does not appear in `git diff --name-only`). - S5/S6/S7 (check-in refusal/audit, checked_in_at gating, capacity+override audit): N/A -- no check-in code touched; confirmed `handlers/checkin.ts` absent from the diff's file list. - S8 (exactly one AuditLog row per status change): N/A for new writes -- `getMyRegistrations` writes nothing; the only write reachable from this diff's own surface (withdraw, via the reused button) goes through the unchanged `withdrawRegistration`, whose single `writeAuditLog` call was already verified at REQ-022's original gate and is untouched here. - S9/S10 (notification idempotency, marketing/transactional split): N/A -- no notification code added or touched by this diff. - S11 (no PII in plaintext logs): grepped the full diff for `console.` -- exactly one occurrence, `console.warn` in `handlers/my.test.ts`'s DB-unavailable skip message (an infra warning naming the connection string, not any user's PII) -- read it directly, confirmed no phone/email/name ever appears in a log call anywhere in the diff. - S12 (exports role-gated and audited): N/A -- no export functionality in this diff. - S13 (deletion anonymizes, preserves aggregates): N/A, and re-confirmed rather than assumed -- `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/` produces zero output; no migration, no `ALTER TABLE`/`CREATE TABLE` anywhere in the diff (grepped). Matches the design doc's own claim (REQ-024.md's opening section) that no schema change is needed, verified independently rather than trusted. - S14 (publication consent default-off): N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched; `/my` never reads or renders Profile fields at all (confirmed: `MyRegistrationListItem` carries no profile field, only registration/event/chapter columns). Build/lint/test, all run by me: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web `` LCP warnings (unchanged from every prior gate on this branch). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (Next.js + apps/bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running on 55432) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, including my.test.ts's AC1-AC5 suite and qr.test.ts's real-decode suite. Verdict: PASS. No new S1-S14 concern found; the /my-specific adversarial scenario (forged callback_data enumeration) and the new QR-content-leak check both resolve clean, verified independently rather than assumed to transfer from REQ-022's prior review.

evidence.s3_adversarial_forged_callback: CONFIRMED SAFE -- withdrawRegistration re-reads the target row fresh by id alone inside its own transaction (no userId in the WHERE clause) and only then applies decideWithdrawOutcome's ownership check; a real-but-not-owned id and a nonexistent id take structurally identical paths (same query shape, no write, one sync decision) and withdraw.ts's switch maps both 'not-owner' and 'not-found' to the identical reply string. Verified experimentally, not just read: forged-callback reply text was byte-equal between the two cases, no victim PII leaked, victim's row unmodified.
evidence.qr_content_leak_check: CONFIRMED CLEAN -- renderCheckInQrPng's only inputs are botUsername and qrToken; its only output is the literal deep-link template, verified by an actual PNG decode (jsqr+pngjs) in qr.test.ts, re-run by me. The caption sent alongside it reuses only the row's own already-S3-scoped fields; no raw token or other-user data appears as visible text.
evidence.dependency_risk: npm audit (both default and --omit=dev) reports 0 known vulnerabilities for qrcode@1.5.4/jsqr@1.4.0/pngjs@7.0.0 and their transitive tree, as of this review's run. Not exhaustive against future disclosures -- flagged as a standing gap for future dependency-audit tooling, not treated as fully out of scope since a real check was possible and was run.
